landing.title: Make your CV and website tell one strong story
landing.subtitle: Porichoy checks your website and your CV, shows the exact line behind every problem, asks you a few questions, and writes a stronger CV in your own words. In English or Bangla.

stats.label: AI models: one writes, one verifies

steps.title: Upload or paste a link
steps.body: Upload your CV as a PDF, or enter your website address. No sign-up, no passwords.

steps.title: See every problem
steps.body: Each problem points to the exact line, explains why it hurts you, and how to fix it.

steps.title: Answer, then download
steps.body: The AI asks a few questions, writes a better CV, and a second AI checks it for invented facts.

features.title: Evidence for every finding
features.body: Every problem quotes your CV or site word for word. If the quote isn't really there, the finding is dropped.

features.title: A second AI checks every rewrite
features.body: A separate model rejects any new CV that adds clients, numbers or dates you never gave.

features.title: Scores you can explain
features.body: Scores come from fixed rules, so the same content always gets the same score.

features.title: Questions, not guesses
features.body: Missing a number? The AI asks you instead of making one up.

features.title: Real website checks
features.body: We crawl your site, read its SEO tags and structured data, and measure speed with Google PageSpeed.

features.title: Private by default
features.body: Reports are kept for 6 hours, then deleted. You can delete yours any time.

https.title: Uses HTTPS
https.why: Browsers mark plain-HTTP sites as “Not secure”, and Google ranks HTTPS sites higher.
https.fix: Turn on a free SSL certificate in your hosting panel (most hosts offer Let's Encrypt) and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

status_ok.title: Homepage loads cleanly
status_ok.why: Errors or long redirect chains slow visitors down and can stop Google from indexing the page.
status_ok.fix: Make your homepage return a normal 200 response with at most 2 redirects.

robots_allowed.title: Search engines are allowed in
robots_allowed.why: If robots.txt blocks your homepage, Google won't show your site in search.
robots_allowed.fix: Remove any “Disallow: /” rule for all user agents in robots.txt.

sitemap.title: Has an XML sitemap
sitemap.why: A sitemap helps Google find all your pages, especially new ones.
sitemap.fix: Generate sitemap.xml (most site builders and SEO plugins do this) and list it in robots.txt.

canonical.title: Has a canonical link
canonical.why: Without it, Google may treat versions of the same page as duplicates and split your ranking.
canonical.fix: Add <link rel="canonical" href="https://yoursite.com/"> to each page's <head>.

viewport.title: Mobile-friendly viewport
viewport.why: Without it, phones show a tiny zoomed-out desktop page. Most visitors are on phones.

indexable.title: Homepage can be indexed
indexable.why: A “noindex” tag hides the page from Google completely.
indexable.fix: Remove noindex from the robots meta tag on pages you want found.

html_lang.title: Page language is set
html_lang.why: It helps search engines and screen readers handle your text correctly.
html_lang.fix: Add lang="en" (or lang="bn") to the <html> tag.

title_length.title: Clear, unique page title
title_length.why: Google shows the title in search results. Short or generic titles like “Home” get skipped.
title_length.fix: Use 30–60 characters with your name and main service, and a different title on each page.

meta_description.title: Good meta description
meta_description.why: It's the snippet under your title in Google. A good one gets more clicks.
meta_description.fix: Write 70–160 characters saying who you help and how.

single_h1.title: Exactly one main heading
single_h1.why: One clear h1 tells visitors and Google what the page is about.
single_h1.fix: Keep one <h1> per page and use <h2>/<h3> for the rest.

img_alt.title: Images have alt text
img_alt.why: Alt text helps blind visitors and lets Google understand your images.
img_alt.fix: Add a short description to every meaningful image's alt attribute.

key_pages.title: Links to contact or services
key_pages.why: Visitors who can't find how to hire you will leave.
key_pages.fix: Link to a Contact and a Services or Portfolio page from the homepage.

open_graph.title: Looks good when shared
open_graph.why: Open Graph tags control the preview on Facebook, LinkedIn and WhatsApp.
open_graph.fix: Add og:title, og:description and og:image tags.

jsonld_valid.title: Has valid structured data
jsonld_valid.why: Structured data (JSON-LD) helps Google show rich results and understand who you are.
jsonld_valid.fix: Paste the JSON-LD we generated in the Content & trust section into your <head>.

schema_type.title: Describes a person or business
schema_type.why: A Person or Organization type connects your site to your name in Google's knowledge graph.
schema_type.fix: Use @type Person (for individuals) or Organization / LocalBusiness.

same_as.title: Links your other profiles
same_as.why: sameAs links tell Google your LinkedIn, GitHub and other profiles belong to you.
same_as.fix: Add a sameAs list with your profile URLs to your structured data.

lighthouse.title: Fast overall (Lighthouse)
lighthouse.why: Slow sites lose visitors; over half leave if a page takes 3+ seconds on a phone.
lighthouse.fix: Compress images (WebP), remove unused scripts and plugins, and use caching or a CDN.

lcp.title: Main content appears fast (LCP)
lcp.why: Largest Contentful Paint shows how fast the main content appears. Google wants 2.5 s or less.
lcp.fix: Shrink the hero image, preload it, and avoid render-blocking scripts.

inp.title: Responds quickly to taps
inp.why: Slow responses make a site feel broken. Google wants 200 ms or less.
inp.fix: Reduce heavy JavaScript and third-party widgets; defer what isn't needed at first.

cls.title: Layout doesn't jump (CLS)
cls.why: Content that jumps while loading causes mis-taps. Google wants 0.1 or less.
cls.fix: Set width and height on images and reserve space for ads and embeds.

who.title: Clear who you are
who.why: Visitors hire people they can identify: a real name, photo and what you do.
who.fix: Put your name, role and who you help at the top of the homepage.

proof.title: Shows proof of experience
proof.why: Case studies, results and testimonials are what convince clients.
proof.fix: Add 2–3 projects with the problem, what you did and the result, plus a client quote.

contact.title: Easy to contact
contact.why: If contacting you takes effort, leads go elsewhere.
contact.fix: Show email or a contact form, plus your city or service area, on every page.

recent.title: Shows recent work
recent.why: Undated or old work makes visitors wonder if you're still active.
recent.fix: Add dates to projects or posts and show something from the last 6 months.

text_selectable.title: Text can be read by software
text_selectable.why: Applicant tracking systems (ATS) can't read scanned or image-only CVs, so they get rejected automatically.
text_selectable.fix: Export your CV from Word or Google Docs as PDF instead of scanning or photographing it.

page_count.title: 1–2 pages long
page_count.why: Recruiters spend seconds on a first look; long CVs bury your best work.
page_count.fix: Keep to 1 page (under 5 years' experience) or 2 pages at most.

length_words.title: Right amount of text
length_words.why: Too little looks thin; too much is hard to skim.

standard_headings.title: Standard section headings
standard_headings.why: ATS software looks for headings like Experience, Education and Skills to sort your CV.
standard_headings.fix: Use plain headings: Summary, Experience, Projects, Education, Skills.

contact_email.title: Has an email address
contact_email.why: Recruiters can't reach you without it.
contact_email.fix: Add a professional email (e.g. firstname.lastname@gmail.com) at the top.

contact_phone.title: Has a phone number
contact_phone.why: Many recruiters call or WhatsApp first.
contact_phone.fix: Add your number with the country code, e.g. +880 17…

contact_linkedin.title: Links your LinkedIn
contact_linkedin.why: Most recruiters check LinkedIn before an interview.
contact_linkedin.fix: Add your linkedin.com/in/… address next to your email.

bullets_quantified.title: Bullets include numbers
bullets_quantified.why: Numbers (clients, users, time saved, sales) prove impact and stand out.
bullets_quantified.fix: Add a number to at least 4 in 10 bullets. The AI will ask you for them.

date_consistency.title: One date format
date_consistency.why: Mixed formats look careless and can confuse ATS software.
date_consistency.fix: Use one style everywhere, e.g. “Jan 2022 – Mar 2024”.

personal_info.title: No unnecessary personal details
personal_info.why: Date of birth, religion, marital status or parents' names aren't needed abroad and can lead to bias.
personal_info.fix: Remove the Personal Information section; keep name, contact and location.

summary_strong.title: Strong summary at the top
summary_strong.why: A clear 2–3 line summary tells the recruiter in seconds why to keep reading.
summary_strong.fix: Say who you are, what you offer and one proof point. Drop generic “career objective” lines.

action_verbs.title: Bullets start with action verbs
action_verbs.fix: Start every bullet with a strong past-tense verb.

achievements.title: Shows results, not just duties
achievements.why: Employers hire for results. Duties only say what the job was.
achievements.fix: For each role, write what changed because of your work.

spelling_grammar.title: No spelling or grammar mistakes
spelling_grammar.why: Small errors suggest carelessness and can get a CV rejected.
spelling_grammar.fix: Fix the errors found and read the CV aloud once before sending.
